title: Core Vocabulary: Opinion Phrases for Writing and Speaking

topic_snapshot.description: Essential functional language to clearly state, defend, and nuance your opinions in IELTS Tasks.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: A person who publicly supports or recommends a particular cause or policy (noun); to publicly support (verb).
key_vocabulary_bank.example: I strongly advocate for stricter environmental regulations.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A confident person standing at a podium giving a passionate speech.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Accept or admit the existence or truth of.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: While I acknowledge the benefits of technology, we must also consider its drawbacks.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: Two people nodding in agreement during a serious discussion.

collocation_builder.meaning: To have a very strong conviction.
collocation_builder.example: I firmly believe that education is the key to solving poverty.
It is widely recognized that smoking causes severe health issues.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: I am of the opinion that / From my perspective
upgrade_section.example: From my perspective, the disadvantages far outweigh the advantages.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: It is often argued that / It is a common belief that
upgrade_section.example: It is often argued that university education should be free for everyone.

sentence_frames: While it is valid to argue that [Clause], I am of the opinion that [Clause].
It is fundamentally important to recognize that [Clause].

ielts_usage_examples.writing_example: It is widely recognized that automation will displace many manual workers. While I acknowledge this challenge, I firmly believe that technology will ultimately create new, highly-skilled jobs.
ielts_usage_examples.speaking_example: From my perspective, working from home is fantastic. I mean, I acknowledge that you miss out on office banter, but the flexibility is just unbeatable.

common_mistakes: Writing 'According to me' instead of 'In my opinion'. (Only use 'According to' for third-party sources).

quiz.question: Which phrase is the most formal academic upgrade for 'Many people say'?
quiz.explanation: 'It is often argued that' is a highly formal, objective way to introduce a common opinion in an essay.
